skill.name: building-mcp-servers
skill.description: Guides developers through building Model Context Protocol servers for external APIs and services. It covers TypeScript and Python patterns, tool design, authentication, deployment, and evaluation workflows.
skill.summary: Build MCP servers with practical TypeScript, Python, deployment, and evaluation guidance.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, TypeScript template literals, placeholder URLs, and placeholder credential names. Confirmed issues are limited to security-relevant deployment guidance around broad HTTP exposure and the evaluation harness path that can launch user-specified commands. No evidence found of prompt injection text or malicious exfiltration intent.

remediation.issue: Broad HTTP listener and host-acceptance examples can be copied into production deployments.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit production guidance to restrict bind addresses, allowed hosts, CORS origins, and network access unless behind a trusted gateway.

remediation.issue: The evaluation harness launches a user-specified stdio command for local MCP server testing.
remediation.suggestion: Document that users must only run trusted commands and should avoid passing sensitive environment variables to untrusted servers.

remediation.issue: Credential examples use placeholder API keys and tokens across several references.
remediation.suggestion: Use clearly fake placeholders and remind users to use scoped test credentials instead of production secrets.

semantic_findings.title: User-Specified Command Execution in Evaluation Harness
semantic_findings.description: The evaluation harness accepts a command and arguments from the user and passes them to the MCP stdio client. This is intended for testing local MCP servers, but it can execute arbitrary local programs if used with untrusted input.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The argparse options collect a user-provided command and arguments, and connections.py passes them into StdioServerParameters. The behavior is legitimate for evaluation but still creates local command execution risk.

semantic_findings.title: Permissive Internal HTTP Deployment Pattern
semantic_findings.description: The TaskFlow reference describes an internal MCP server with upstream authentication and shows wildcard CORS settings. If copied outside a controlled internal network, this pattern can expose tools too broadly.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly states auth is handled upstream and the shown CORS wrapper allows all origins and headers. The risk depends on deployment context, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Building MCP servers requires careful choices for tools, schemas, transport, authentication, and testing. This skill provides practical patterns for creating servers that work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to plan MCP tools around external service workflows and API coverage.
Provides TypeScript MCP SDK patterns for tools, schemas, transports, and structured responses.
Provides Python FastMCP patterns using Pydantic models, async HTTP clients, and annotations.
Describes Docker, streamable HTTP, stdio, and health-check deployment considerations.
Includes an evaluation harness for testing MCP servers with XML question-and-answer files.
Gives checklists for naming, pagination, error handling, response formatting, and tool safety hints.
limitations: It does not generate a complete production server without service-specific API details.
It includes example code that must be adapted and reviewed before deployment.
It assumes the user understands how to protect API credentials and network endpoints.
The evaluation harness can run user-specified local commands and should only be used with trusted inputs.

use_cases.title: Create a New API MCP Server
use_cases.description: Plan tools, schemas, response formats, and transports for a service integration.

use_cases.title: Review MCP Tool Quality
use_cases.description: Check naming, annotations, pagination, errors, and output structure before release.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Server Effectiveness
use_cases.description: Create read-only evaluation questions and run them against a local or remote MCP server.

prompt_templates.title: Plan My MCP Server
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new integration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan an MCP server for this service. Identify core tools, inputs, outputs, authentication needs, and transport choice.

prompt_templates.title: Design Tool Schemas
prompt_templates.prompt: Design MCP tool schemas for these API workflows. Include names, descriptions, validation rules, annotations, and response formats.

prompt_templates.title: Review Implementation Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my MCP server implementation against the skill guidance. Focus on type safety, pagination, error handling, auth, and deployment risk.

prompt_templates.title: Build Evaluation Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Create evaluation questions for this MCP server. Make them read-only, realistic, independently verifiable, stable, and useful for finding tool gaps.

output_examples.input: A request to build an MCP server for a project management API.
output_examples.output: A tool plan with project, task, user, and search operations, plus schema and pagination recommendations.

output_examples.input: A TypeScript MCP server draft that returns large unfiltered responses.
output_examples.output: A review that recommends limits, offsets, structured responses, clearer errors, and stricter validation.

output_examples.input: A request for evaluation tasks for a read-only GitHub-style MCP server.
output_examples.output: A set of stable questions with exact expected answers and notes about avoiding destructive operations.

best_practices: Use service-prefixed tool names, strict input validation, and clear read-only or destructive annotations.
Return focused responses with pagination, structured content, and actionable error messages.
Test servers with realistic read-only evaluations before exposing them to production agents.
anti_patterns: Do not expose broad HTTP listeners without trusted network controls and host restrictions.
Do not pass production credentials into example commands or untrusted evaluation servers.
Do not create vague tools that hide side effects or return unbounded external API data.

faq.question: Does this skill build the server automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides implementation and review. The user still provides service-specific API details and code changes.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers TypeScript with the MCP SDK and Python with FastMCP.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it include deployment guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It discusses stdio, streamable HTTP, Docker, health checks, and transport security.

faq.question: Does it handle authentication?
faq.answer: It gives patterns for API keys, forwarded tokens, service tokens, and upstream authentication designs.

faq.question: What should I review before publishing a server?
faq.answer: Review credential handling, network exposure, tool side effects, input validation, pagination, and evaluation coverage.
